TripMate

Captured from the React Native client on an iPhone 17, against live data and a real generated itinerary — not mockups. Shared to collect design feedback and ideas.

The data is live. A real generated itinerary for Lisbon, live geocoding as you type, and live POI search from OpenStreetMap — no fixtures, no lorem, no placeholder prices. The design system is Kiln, shipped 2026-09-08 and documented in DESIGN.md.

Palette
  • Kiln Jade#28B981Action, and only action — never a label, never a figure.
  • Kiln Gold#E9B44CMoney, and only money. A figure is information, not an invitation.
  • Ember Coral#E4553FOver-plan and failure. Spent only on what cannot happen.
  • The one slate#1C1A18Every panel, pill, badge and sheet — this colour at some alpha.
  • Ground#121110The single warm near-black the whole app sits on.
  • Paper#F7F5F2Body text, and text over any dark surface.
Type
  • MelodramaDisplay serif, one weightMastheads, destinations, the statement on each screen.
  • System sansThe platform's own faceAll body and UI text — which is what buys Dynamic Type and Android font scaling. A custom face here would freeze it.
  • TabularFiguresMoney, counts and dates, so columns of numbers line up.

Changing it2

Two ways in, both conversational.

How to read the palette. Three colours, one meaning each: jade acts and only acts, gold counts money and only money, coral is kept for something that cannot happen. Everything else is warm paper on a single near-black slate. If a screen here seems to break that, it is worth saying — that is exactly what this board is for.

One thing already known. Two screens are absent: the generation screen, because capturing it would have meant spending a real model run, and the wizard’s Review step, which only renders populated when the wizard is walked in sequence.
